title: Clean Emitting Call Simulation
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $f$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $M$ computes $f$ on every Boolean input $a$ within $T(|a|)$ steps. Then there are a finite Boolean Turing machine $C$ with at least one work tape, two of its states called entry and exit, and a natural number $c$, such that for every pair of Boolean words $x,a$ there is a positive integer $t\le c(T(|a|)+|a|+|f(a)|+1)$ for which the run of $C$ from the configuration with input $x$, state entry, and $a$ on tape zero (all other tapes blank) has not entered exit at any positive time before $t$, and at time $t$ is in state exit with the same tape contents and head positions as that initial configuration, while its output is $f(a)$.
hypotheses_covered: A function $f$ from Boolean words to Boolean words
$M$ computes $f(a)$ on every Boolean input $a$ within $T(|a|)$ steps
The constructed machine has a positive number of work tapes
Every pair of Boolean words $x,a$ has a positive time $t$ bounded by $c(T(|a|)+|a|+|f(a)|+1)$
The exit state is absent at every positive time before $t$
At time $t$ the configuration has exit state, the initial tape contents and head positions, and output $f(a)$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a bundled finite machine computing a function $f$ on Boolean words in time
$T$. Then there are a machine $C$ with a positive number of work tapes, control states
called entry and exit, and a constant $c$ such that for every native input $x$ and
argument $a$: starting $C$ at the canonical seam in the entry state with $a$ as the sole
tape-resident word, there is a positive time $t \le c\,(T(|a|) + |a| + |f(a)| + 1)$,
before which the exit state is never visited, at which $C$ is exactly at the entry seam
with exit control and physical output $f(a)$: the argument preserved on its tape, all
scratch restored, and the computed word emitted.
